title: It's Guess and Hope
body: Ordered this for my wife to take pictures of birds in our yard using a lens hood and UV filter (both must be purchased separately). It has not been used indoors. The major problem with this camera is the lack of a viewfinder. Pictures must be set up using the small LCD screen on the back of the camera. Unfortunately, when you use the camera outside, the screen shows your own reflection looking back at you and you can't see what you are aiming at. I contacted Kodak customer service to see if anything could be done about this: perhaps a non-reflective coating that could be applied to the screen. This was their reply: "...when hit with sunlight the screen will look black and the only thing you can do is hover your hand over the top of the camera to keep the sun from hitting the LCD screen before pressing the shutter button." Unless you have 3 hands or are using a tripod this is an unworkable solution. The shutter and zoom controls are on the right side of the camera so you hold the camera on the right. You need to steady the camera with your left hand when the zoom is extended because the camera becomes front heavy. Using this camera is like standing in a crowd and holding your cell phone over your head to try to take a picture of something you can't really see. Sometimes you get a good picture, most times you don't. It's not point and shoot - it's guess and hope.

title: Far improved over the D7100
body: Just a short review, more of a user experience. I bought the D7500 for a month long trip to Europe. I was replacing a D7100 that had some nagging problems that often left me less than satisfied (It had been dropped - and repaired - early in its life, but was never as good as I expected). Anyway, I filled 4-5 64 Gig memory cards on the trip, and I have to say that this camera is far better than my old one. The low light abilities are awesome, and on the few instances where I needed to take a picture hand held in low light with some depth of field, ISO 16000 was a very viable option. Not noise free, but better than ISO 6400 on the older camera. Other features that made the user experience better: I could easily transfer pictures to my phone - very important to my wife and convenient for sharing or posting to Facebook when traveling without a computer. The connection to the phone also meant that I could share the phone's GPS with the camera and therefore get location tags on every photo. This worked very well, though it is possible that it negatively affects the phone's battery - but my phone is old and it is hard to really tell. (I think the automatic download was more detrimental to the phone battery, and it took a little searching to figure out how to turn off automatic downloads for every photo). As for the camera battery, it was also good, though again, the automatic download seemed to affect it a lot, as did a lot of activity on the display. The tilting screen was useful to have, but not as useful as a fully articulating screen (like the D5300). The touch screen was awesome, and made it VERY easy to check critical focus and work with the menu - even with gloves on. I was in a cold weather environment, so I had gloves on much of the time. These gloves had something on each finger that would let it work with an iPhone, and therefore it worked just as well with he camera. I liked the feature where you could use the live preview and touch the screen where you wanted it to be in focus, and it would refocus and take the shot.

title: Nikon D5000 is a great camera to learn photography with !
body: I received the Nikon D5000 - VERY QUICKLY - via an Amazon.com dealer and was able to hit the ground running. I knew NOTHING (and I mean NOTHING) about photography (F-stops, aperture size, and shutter speeds meant nothing to me 4 weeks ago), but with the great documentation provided with the D5000 (along with lots of great web-based tutorials) I was able to have intelligent conversations with much-more experienced photographers within the first week. Indoor pics are a challenge for the beginning (because it's all about light, light, light) but close attention to the features for the D5000 will help to make this much easier. Pictures that I thought would be difficult to make good-quality (like late night, long shutter shots) ended up being the easiest to create and the starter lens that comes with the D5000 takes great pics out of the box. Do yourself a favor, and use cambridgeincolour.com along with the (multi-lingual) User's Manual provided. You will be taking great shots in no time. I've learned how to take advantage of both deep and shallow depths-of-field easily with this little wonder, and the quality of pics taken with the Portrait-Setting will make any novice happy. Any photographer will need some patience, but be sure (if you first buy only the body) to get the 18-55mm and 55-200mm Nikkor lenses at a minimum. The long lense will expand your creativity several-fold. You'll find the D5000 runs seemingly forever on a charge of its modular Lithium-Ion battery (the battery is a real workhorse too, rated at over 1 Ah). You will love how the D5000 feels in your hand as well as the multiangle LCD display (that can be rotated to face into the camera to protect it, or rotated to sit inside the body, but facing out for easy continuous use). I'm told they sell LCD protectors so do yourself a favor (as I plan to) and get one, as well as UV filters (if not for utility's sake, then to protect your expensive lenses, since a $20 filter is a lot cheaper to replace than a $200 - or more - lens). The best advice I can give is, practice with this thing a lot, read the manual through (it's enjoyable reading though this is a complex little device) and share your shots with others to get an idea of how well you're doing. Oh, yeah, and get a tripod - it opens up a whole new level of picture-taking. Your photographer friends (if they're anything like mine) will be mostly helpful and encouraging, and will offer advice (even without being prompted). Avoid those who offer destructive advice but listen to everyone else. Take from them what you need and keep learning on this greater teaching camera !

title: Makes Hot coffee
body: I bought this exact coffee maker about 3 months ago and I haven’t had any issues or problems with it so I decided to get a second one for my vacation home. The coffee maker is compact and looks nice on my counter. The instruction manual has straightforward step by step instructions for first time use and for normal coffee brewing. However, there are a couple of things in the instruction manual that I disagree with. First, it says “the appliance can be used by children 8 years old and above if they’ve been given supervision or instruction.” I can’t imagine letting my 8 year old grandson use my coffee maker or why I would want him to. Also, it says you should unplug and thoroughly clean all parts of the coffee maker daily. That’s probably a good thing to do but I have only been cleaning mine periodically. And for clarification, #3 under Normal Brewing says to use one level spoon of coffee for each cup. This should say one level Tablespoon for each cup of coffee. Other than those things I found the instruction manual to be helpful and clear.

I not only highly recommend this product but also the Black+Decker coffee grinder as well. Imagine spending $200 on a Cuisinart coffee machine that doesn't even burr your coffee beans, but then you could buy this coffee machine and their coffee grinder and pay less than half the price and less hassle. I swear by this coffee machine and highly recommend it.

title: Few quirks but it’s good!
body: We bought this to replace our dinosaur Keurig. We had the OG silver, bulky, heavy Keurig. It lasted us a lifetime then died a sudden death. We actually mourned! We have a camper now so I bought this new mini to be a space saver. I like it. I don’t love it yet but I like it. It’s small, lightweight and does the job. It splatters quite a bit, so we drape a lightweight kitchen rag over it while it brews. I’ve also noticed it doesn’t push out all the water every brew. After each brew we immediately remove the pod and toss it. Then randomly I open it later and find the pod area filled with water. Where does this water come from?? Tapping the brew button forces that water to be purged but I have to know why it’s there! It never seems like our cup of coffee is lacking a couple tablespoons so I just don’t know. Maybe a small bit is held back each brew until it creates enough to send it to the pod area. I’m perplexed. Also, if I brew plain water for tea after we have brewed coffee, I have to flush it out with 2 cycles of water or my tea is yucky, ashtray smelling tea. It really clings to that coffee smell!! That being said, love the size and weight, it brews really hot, pretty darn fast and the color is cute. So, 4 stars.

Another call resolved that when I pointed out the receipt showed I purchased the item on Amazon and I told the Agent I had additional proof the unit was shipped directly by Amazon. My claim was then approved and I received a brand new replacement with all accessories in about one week.

title: Nice Coffee Maker as Expected from Keurig
body: I received my Keurig K-Elite Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker yesterday so I don't have a lot of use to review it by but I will say that having had several Keurig coffee makers in the past I like the look, feel and utility of this model. I read several reviews prior to purchase that claimed the temperature of the brew was not as hot as was set in the machine. I experienced the same and wanted to understand it better. I have my machine set at 190 for the temperature. I used a calibrated Thermapen ONE Thermometer, the one chefs use and rely on, and the temp of the coffee in my cup right after brewing completed was 158. Then I measured the brew as it exits the machine but before it got into my cup and it was 187. Turns out my ceramic cup was at room temperature and some of the heat from the brew was used up to heat my cup, which lowered the resultant temp of the coffee in my cup. Bottom line: my machine is very close to the temp I set for the brew. If I preheat my cup the coffee in my cup will be very close to what I have my machine set to. So I am happy and my coffee maker is performing as specified.

title: The O.G.!!!! THE BEST
body: This is by far the best quality espresso machine at a reasonable price point for your home. My ex husband's father bought us this machine in 2012 and it works perfectly still in 2026. I bought my own machine recently because my ex husband kept our first machine when he moved out. My new version of the same Breville Barista Express is just as awesome and easy to set up and get started as the old machine was. Much to my excitement, I guessed correctly on my first try with the grind size and grind amount. I brewed the perfect espresso with an amazing crema head. I was historically a barista while in college, and this tiny little inexpensive machine makes espressos and lattes just as well as any Starbucks barista can. I waited until this machine went on sale for $500 on Christmas Day and bought it. It also goes to that price on Black Friday or cyber monday. Fun fact, it was $500 in 2012, so it has not increased in price when you wait for the sale price. When you think about how much you would spend at Starbucks everyday, this machine pays for itself in less than 6 months. I'm a huge fan of the hot water feature, as I love to make Americanos. In case anyone wants to know, I use the brand of coffee called Purity, and love the "Ease" flavor. The beans work so well with this machine. I also highly recommend buying the Breville knock box for your grind bricks. This particular machine also comes with something that the old one did not, which is a spill proof topper for when you are grinding. It clicks right on and prevents you from spilling precious ground coffee, but has a wide mouth for easily tamping all of the grounds down before you remove it and brew the espresso. I just love this machine. If you do like lattes, the frother works so well with any type of milk. I have used almond milk, soy milk, and regular cow's milk. It's easy to clean if you immediately wipe it down with a wet paper towel. I can't say enough awesome things about it. There are so many others like this machine, but this one is the best.

title: Full-featured, high quality home machine, but, if I had to do over again...
body: This is the first espresso machine I've ever owned. I purchased it this Spring (2020) because, like many of you, I needed to stop going out. I didn't know much about home brewing espresso, but I have lots of Breville products, and I thought this would be a good entry-level machine., I liked that it had all of the features I needed in a one-stop solution, but would still allow me to make "real" espresso, not the stuff that shoots of a pod, which I typically dislike. Armed with nothing more than the instructions it came with, power, water, and beans, I was able to brew espresso good enough to keep me from going into withdrawal, but typically not delicious, and appreciably less enjoyable than my favorite baristas in my favorite cafes. I also wasted a lot of beans in the process. After about 10 days of this bumbling around, I decided to start researching how to get better performance, learning a lot of coffee science along the way, and over the next few months, my technique and results improved, but ultimately plateaued at a point where I felt my home-brewed espresso was now generally better than my favorite baristas - but still not consistent - one day I could make a perfect shot, with all of the lovely sweetness and velvety texture of great espresso, with little or no extraction defect, but then the next day, doing the exact same thing, would get something uneven and over- or under- extracted, and not as good. I was not exactly sure what the variable was, but I suspected it was the grind consistency, since by now I had become very practiced at everything else.

title: Great machine for coffee lovers and beginner baristas and the whole family
body: This is our first espresso machine. We love the professional look of this product and its easy to keep it clean. I like the little pop up sign when the drip tray is full. We have had it for just over a month and only now really starting to understand how to use it properly and pull perfect shots and get the milk frothed properly, thanks to a number of good instructional videos on line. It's still a bit hard to predict how it's going to come out as small variations in puck compression etc can make a difference and I'm working on my cappuccino art skills. The machine heats up quickly, but it's recommended to turn it on in advance and warm the cup on the top grill. My daughter LOVEs the frother for the most amazing hot chocolate using ordinary carnation hot chocolate powder. This is a great machine if you want the satisfaction of pulling your own shots and frothing your own milk. I am really happy we didn't buy a fully automatic, where's the fun in that? I am also very happy that it has a built in grinder but wish that a water line could be installed to replace the tank. We unknowingly ran out of water once because it was hard to see the water line, but other than that I don't know enough about other machines to say anything bad. We still have our regular coffee maker along side this one for the daily grab and go.

title: Almost perfect, but still Awesome!
body: So, like you all ,I've been a coffeeholic for many years. Like you ,I've struggled to have a decent maker in my kitchen. I recently finished up with my Cuisinart mod#CHW-12. Had it for 5yrs. It got to point of no longer producing a well tasting cup. We did the Vinigar cleaning etc. So, i spent MANY hours searching online for a decent Maker. Problem was the abundance of poor reviews encompassing many manufacturers! It's now 2018 and we have trouble creating a Kit Coffee Brewer thats decent! I did a switch and desired a maker that will produce a single cup as wife n i both have coffee at different times and mostly need the one 16oz cup. In searching for the 12cup Carafe / or single cup Maker ,my choices became limited. Read the reviews and pulled the trigger on this. It's only been 1wk now but i can honestly state that it is the BEST maker I've ever used! I ran a full 12cup Carafe first off, thn dumped. Then did same for the single cup side. ( full 14oz). Then ran 12cups clean water through for both. Then did the Coffee that I'll drink. No issues. Had to play round wth the exact amount of grounds for the single side so to get the outcome i desired. Has clock, easy to pre prog., and, the single side will turn off when done. The Carafe side will stay on (hot plate) for 2hrs after brewing complete. You can simply press On/Off button to turn off anytime. For those who have an over-spilling issue with the grounds within the gold filter basket?, you are using TOO MANY grounds! The single side comes with a gold reusable filter which also encompasses two - Level markers. One is min and the other is Max. If you fill above the Max level, WELL, overflow of grounds will prob. occur. On the Amazon site you'll see the Reusable filter for the Carafe side in " frequently ordered with". I also ordered that as i don't like paper filters. It performs well. Water level for Carafe is helpful. It's towards the right rear, on the side. It's accurate. Brew time for 12 cups was good. I've learned to warm up my Mug when using single side as it is not as hot as Carafe as no hot plate for the Mug. I use single side to run water for tea as well. What would make this model perfect? If it sounded out a tone when brewing is complete. It also has No charcoal filter as with my Cuisinart. No biggie as i always have used filtered water to begin with. Coffee is better when there's no Chlorine in the H2O! Filling either the Carafe or single side is easy and Max level markers are visible enough to get it right. Carafe pours very well and i like that the Carafe lid stays attached as u simply press thumb to open but it's not required to pour. Single side grounds chamber pulls out easily. Single side has a bottom (under mug/cup) that reverses to then become a elevator to bring cup higher if you'd like. I brewed a cup at lowest level without any spill or splatter. It drips slow enough that i don't believe i need to elevate my mug. This model also looks fantastic, Beautiful! Has a "Bold" brew mode for both Carafe n Sing. The brewing is slower, so u gt a richer brew. Light on clock only on when unit is ON. Has seperate green light that indicates you are using "Program" mode. I don't use "Pods" but if i did the manual states that "Senseo" Pods will work. Note that unit will only brew one side at a time. It cannot brew both sides at once. Very pleased so far. If any issues I'll update here. P.s. if Manufacturer reads this, you may want to consider modifying so to have an end of brew audible tone! Jst a thought. Update!; 1/5/18. Jst did 2 Lg mugs for me ( nine- 8oz cups), using Carafe of course. Wife then needed to do her single 14oz using of course the Single serv side. When throwing the slide switch over to Single, it turns off the Carafe side. So, yeah, hot plate under Carafe is still hot, but, it's now off. So, in future, wife does her single, first, then i do Carafe. UPDATE ; 1/22/18- 3wks now and NO ISSUES! When removing coffee filled Carafe, absolutely no spilling onto hot plate. The spring loaded valve above, performing well. Reviewers having the Hot plate discoloration or burning may be turning unit on with a Hot plate thats dirty. I make sure plate is clean /dry before and after ea. use. I make sure bottom of Carafe is clean/ dry as well. Wife using single serve ea. day and says " best cup of Coffee ever"! Update; 4/17/21. NO issues, all still good. UPDATE!!! - 10/10/21- So, finally I'm now considering buying a new one of these as this one is intermittently not pumping enough water up and into Coffee basket. About 12× now in past 6mon's I've had to pour out Carafe into another cup, place Carafe back, then pour my Coffee,(that looks like Tea), into the grinds basket and do a Double Drip, sometimes twice to get color I wish. I got roughly 3.5 years out of this Maker. I guess that's good considering Everything's made in Cheapo China. If/when I buy a new one, I'll post back. Have a good Coffee! UPDATE: 11/14/21. So, I purchased this exact model once again on 10/12/21. After 1 month, I can honestly state that it's a great difference between original and new. New machine brews perfectly as did the original one up until the 3yr mark. No issues to report with this New Maker( Same model as first one). Pictures here are of 2nd maker,(2021).

title: The "Chevy Malibu Premier" of coffeemakers.
body: It's about what you'd expect for a mid-range Hamilton Beach coffee maker. Normal price of $80 feels a bit steep, but I think it's worth what I paid for it on prime day. It does what it says on the box/product listing and it works better than the dollar store coffeemakers you'd find in an economy hotel room. Looks to be of quality from afar, is somewhat cheap and plastic feeling when you actually use it. Just sturdy enough that I'm not concerned that I'll break it. Single serve and full carafe functions do not share a water tank, and you fill the single serve reservoir with exactly as much water as you want to brew into coffee. Pretty intuitive and I guess pretty standard for this type of coffeemaker. But if you are used to filling the tank once a week and brewing a set 6oz or 8oz this is not that. "Brew Options" button toggles between bold and regular brew strength.... And that's it. There's no way to set brew temperature, but the default temperature is fine. It brews a single serve in about 3 minutes or so. Faster than a drip coffeemaker of yesteryear but if you're expecting it to be as fast as a pod system you're looking in the wrong place. The thing that matters most though is how the coffee comes out, and I have to say it's worth the extra hassle of using loose ground coffee and filters as it's much better than pod-brewed coffee. The slower brew speed results in a better coffee. Much more cost effective than pods too. The reusable single serve filter is surprisingly easy to rinse out. For $50 it's not bad. I would not pay $80 for this. At a price point of $80 I expect to at least be able to choose a brew temperature, even if there are a few pre-sets instead of by-degree. If you can get this for under $60 and you are specifically looking for a coffeemaker that doesn't use pods, then I can recommend it. Otherwise at full price, I don't think it offers enough to differentiate it from other $60 coffeemakers to justify the extra $20. It does have a clock in it and the ability to set a time to automatically start brewing at a set time, which is a feature I really don't use, but for some maybe this will make the $80 asking price worth it as I am not sure if this feature is commonly available in cheaper options.

title: Few quirks but it’s good!
body: We bought this to replace our dinosaur Keurig. We had the OG silver, bulky, heavy Keurig. It lasted us a lifetime then died a sudden death. We actually mourned! We have a camper now so I bought this new mini to be a space saver. I like it. I don’t love it yet but I like it. It’s small, lightweight and does the job. It splatters quite a bit, so we drape a lightweight kitchen rag over it while it brews. I’ve also noticed it doesn’t push out all the water every brew. After each brew we immediately remove the pod and toss it. Then randomly I open it later and find the pod area filled with water. Where does this water come from?? Tapping the brew button forces that water to be purged but I have to know why it’s there! It never seems like our cup of coffee is lacking a couple tablespoons so I just don’t know. Maybe a small bit is held back each brew until it creates enough to send it to the pod area. I’m perplexed. Also, if I brew plain water for tea after we have brewed coffee, I have to flush it out with 2 cycles of water or my tea is yucky, ashtray smelling tea. It really clings to that coffee smell!! That being said, love the size and weight, it brews really hot, pretty darn fast and the color is cute. So, 4 stars.

title: Great Coffee Maker
body: Being old school I have never tasted or owned a Kcup coffee pod before but going on 80 I thought I would splurge so I investigated and read a ton of reviews, even checked out testing of machines of Youtube. I came to the conclusion, I am a single person so a single serve was a good choice. Being overwhelmed with so many bells and whistles on many it was overwhelming. Ease of use and care played a big role in decision making. Choice of size, weight, beeps when ready feature and color became a factor. I chose this particular maker, not solel on reviews but I really loved the looks and simplicity of use. I do not own a coffee mug, I use my vintage coffee CUPS that are just below 6 oz. I read reviews on spattering all over when filling cups and not mugs, it's as simple as using a small ramekin upside down to raise the coffee cup just under the drip. I like the removable water tank for easier filling and cleaning. The unit shuts down after a few minutes and you just press any pad to wake it up. I can get 2 cups of coffee with one kcup using my coffee cup verses a mug. I have never liked mugs as my coffee always got cold before drinking it all and for me a single cup with a saucer is all I need. I never drink coffee while on the go because coffee is a diuretic and can create uncomfortable situations. If your looking for just a coffee maker for the convenience of instant coffee using either the kcup or ground coffee single use without the long wait of a drip, percolator, french press, old or new, then this coffee maker is a wise choice. I also love the small foot print. I bought the 36 kcup organizer and is a perfect base this coffee maker. At some time I will try the Tea and Iced Coffee features. I cannot say enough about this coffee maker, it has changed my mornings completely. I highly recommend purchasing this one for it's looks, simplicity, extra features, ease of use, safety features, cleaning and light weight.

title: Nice brew machine.
body: Just arrived and I brewed my first cup! First thing: it brews quietly. No chugging, or whirring like my old K brand. Second: my coffee was hot and tasted great! Third: It just looks nice. Great space saver. I love, love, LOVE that it they included a reusable pod+filter for using coffee grounds. Very easy to use. Fill up reservoir and plug it in. I don't make iced coffee but my daughter will when she visits, so I'm happy about that function. Water reservoir fits perfectly - no gap between reservoir and machine. Photos show machine is about as wide as a 2L bottle, and about as tall. I removed the drip tray to fit my travel mug (12 oz, 6.5 inches tall). The drip tray is plastic, but the drip try cover is steel (nice). The plastic is a solid, durable quality, much like my K brand. Some 'sputtering' at the end of the brew, which is normal. The machine will shut off automatically when brew is completed. There is no "on-off" button. I will fill out the extra warranty card, because all coffee maker have a life span of their own. Very pleased with this purchase from Twomeow.

title: The best k-cup brewer
body: Don't turn up your nose at the Keurig brewer. It can make decent coffee quickly and you can use your own ground coffee if you want to reduce waste. This brewer looks large but it really is not much bigger than the lesser Keurigs. It is a heavy machine, about 18 pounds. It's mass may be why it is so much quieter than any other Keurig brewer I have tried. The construction is a level above the residential models. The brew chamber operates smoothly and there is an extra pressure plate in the brew head that stabilizes the pod while being clamped. What I enjoy about this machine is its simplicity. I don't have to puzzle over an array of push buttons, most of which I don't care about but require my attention for every brew. Many complain about the lack of 12 oz size which I don't lament at all. That's the size you would select if you want a weak and bitter cup of coffee. There just is not enough coffee in a k-cup to make a decent 12 oz cuppa Joe. I use 8oz exclusively and since that is always the default size all I have to do is press "Brew" after I close the lid. From start of drip to last burst of air it takes about 50 seconds to extract a cup. This speed should ensure a poor cup of coffee but, surpisingly, in the Keurig system it works. Perhaps the slight pressurization of the hot water makes up for the short brew time, I don't really know. I do know the quality pods I use taste great. My favorite brand so far is Peet's. If you use the cheapest, most stale bargain pods you can find you will make awful coffee. I often use the 4oz size without a pod to preheat a cup and to get the brew compartment warmed up and cleaned. In fact, I use the 4oz rinse a lot because a clean machine is important to good coffee. This extra fussiness is not required but I am, by nature, a fussy person. I had tried the Keurig K-1500 and it has no 4oz size among other failings. (I found it to be very noisy and slow to heat. It also can't brew a second cup quickly, it has to heat up again.) I thought the K-1500 would be a cheaper and newer alternative to the older K-155 but it is miles away. Excellent aspects of the K-155 is that you can adjust the temperature within a 10 degree range. My test with an accurate thermometer shows the settings to be accurate. This amazes me because I see many review videos of other Kurig brewers where the temperature never even gets to 180. Keurig nailed the temp adjustment on this machine. I like that I can set the on and off times for the machine. It is ready for me in the morning and it obediently goes off at night. I drink coffee or want hot water all day so I don't use the 2-hour auto off function. I have two complaints. The first is that there is no backup for the time setting. If you momentarily use power the clock shuts down and so does the on/off setting and the auto off if you are using that one. How hard could it have been to include a button cell battery and a simple circuit to keep the clock alive? Very disappointing and annoying. My only other annoyance is the silly display. The little movie is repetitive and conveys information nobody was asking for. Why can't we choose to shut that down or suppress it. Both of these gripes are petty and not of much consequence. This brewer will give you your money's worth in decent quality hot coffee. My previous brewers have had fairly short lives and I am hoping this one will last.

title: ☹️ Super disappointed in my purchase
body: I purchased this Keurig 155 for my home only four months ago and it completely died. For the price I thought this would be a great quality coffee maker for our home that would last awhile….especially when our home averages only about 5-6 cups of coffee daily. I originally had a Keurig K-Cafe Special Edition Coffee maker that we’ve had for ages and works like a champ. The only reason I wanted the Keurig K155 was because of the extra water reservoir capacity. (😖 I should have just continued with my older Keurig and accepted a few extra trips to keep the water reservoir full) The issues started within a week of using the new Keurig K155. First it was the constant “water flow interrupted” warning that “sometimes” would resolve itself if I lifted the water reservoir then reset it back down. This might result in me being able to grab one cup of coffee only to have the water flow interruption warning come up again. I tried descaling it hoping that might help just in case I was sent a refurbished K155 without my knowledge. The descaling didn’t help at all and I just continued to lift the water reservoir up multiple times a week just to remove the warning prompt. Eventually my Keurig K155 died without a warning prompt and the pump just wouldn’t activate. I scoured the internet looking for “solutions” and tried several troubleshooting tips only to result with failure. I was beyond disappointed because this model of Keurig is certainly not cheap. Because it was barely 4 months old I contacted Keurig warranty department to make a claim under the 1 year manufacturers warranty. I had to do several troubleshooting tips over the phone but everything just failed. Keurig did indeed send me a replacement about a week later while I plugged in my older Keurig Special Edition coffee maker waiting for my replacement to arrive. When my replacement Keurig K155 arrived I unboxed it and plugged it in just to see if it would turn on. I saw in the fine print of the warranty information that I could be sent a refurbished K155 so I inspected it closely to see if I could find evidence that I received a refurbished one. It didn’t appear scratched or looked used as far as I could tell. 🤷🏻‍♀️

title: Brews 12 Cups Quickly And No Glass Carafe To Break
body: The Hamilton Beach 47950 BrewStation was purchased to replace my old Hamilton Beach BrewStation that, after 12 years, finally started dripping from the reservoir. Their new design has some pluses and minuses. Too many pluses to list them all, and the minuses are two: 1) it isn't that easy to clean the reservoir and 2) you can't pour from the top of the reservoir into a thermos. My old BrewStation had a spout built into the reservoir and made it easy to brew 10 cups, pour 8 into my thermos and the remaining into my insulated mug. This models reservoir is multiple parts with openings at the top in a few places and is not sealed. So trying to pour of the top of the reservoir just makes a mess and you loose half the coffee down the drain. It require you to use the built in push to pour spout at the bottom of the reservoir. I use a measuring cup with a handle to accomplish what used to be a quick and simple task. It works, but takes more time and means I have another item to wash. Other than that, I love the coffee maker. It brews 12 cups very fast and exactly how I like it. It has a timer for how long the warmer will stay on and is programmable so you can set it up before bed and your coffee will be ready when you wake up. It has an "iced coffee" setting , a "bold" setting and a setting for a small batch of coffee "1-4 cups". If you are in need of a replacement coffee maker or are looking to buy your first one, this is a great choice.

title: Nice brewer, but.....
body: Looks nice, works well. However..... It advertises a removable water filter with measurements on it in the water reservoir for the K cup. This doesn't have that, it has a plastic measurement piece that is screwed into the reservoir, but that's not a deal breaker for me. Love that it does not take forever to brew a 12 cup pot, and that it shuts off after 2 hours rather than burning the coffee in the carafe/pot. I DON'T like that you can't just turn it back on to continue keeping the coffee that is in the pot hot longer. Simply turning the maker back on does not turn the hot plate back on. Also, I don't like that just touching the hour or minute button, even accidently, changes the time on the clock. So, if you're not paying attention, you could change the time without even knowing it! And lastly, the measurement on the pot does NOT match the measurement in the water reservoir. If you put water in the pot up to the 12 cup line, it is only up to the 11 cup line in the reservoir. And if you add water to the reservoir to take it to the 12 cup line, it overfills the pot up to the top of the pot so it is spilling out before you can remove the pot from the hot plate.

title: Prettiest coffee maker I have ever owned!
body: This company has engineered the heck out of this coffee maker! They thought of everything. The size, finish and elegant digital display are the first of many impressive features. It includes a fine mesh filter for the carafe side and on the K cup side they included a fine mesh filter as well. So the single serve side will brew a K cup or your own bulk purchased coffee grounds. The plate that the cup sits on is stainless not plastic and they curved the back side as well. It just shows how much thought was put into the design. I could go on but let me say that I have purchased two Keurig K Duos in two years at $200 each. I said never again but when the second one went I ordered this one and then went to Walmart and ended up getting a K Duo because I had to have one. Now that I have received this beauty I packed up the Keurig. It’s now in the garage. I’ll keep it in case this one goes on the fritz. I’m tempted to get another one of these just to have on hand because I just like it so much! For everyone but especially those who want a beautiful coffee maker for their cute coffee bar; don’t hesitate to grab this or at the least put it on your special occasion wish list. Lastly, I haven’t brewed a cup yet but given the attention to detail that they put into this machine, I have no worries. I’ll have a delicious cup of coffee in the morning. You will not be disappointed if you purchase this coffee maker. It functions differently from the Keurig but I’m so over them. Hope this honest review will help you make a decision. UPDATE: This coffee ot crapped out this morning. It won’t brew. We have softened water so I don’t understand why it only last just under 1 year. We loved this pot so very disappointed!

title: Better than drip coffee maker!
body: For years, I've used drip coffee makers; i.e., Mr. Coffee, Black & Decker, and Mainstays. They served their purpose but I started to worry about the plastic corrosion in these models. I've always ground my coffee beans with a Capresso. Last week, I decided to upgrade to the Presto 02811 and what a noticeable difference!! The coffee pours out several degrees hotter which is a plus for me. I'm not a coffee connoisseur, but the coffee has a much smoother taste to it. I didn't even have to experiment with adjusting the coarseness setting on the bean grinder. Same setting as before. Every day, I make four 6oz. cups of coffee and it takes about 8 minutes to finish brewing. The product came with a few paper filters but I don't think they're necessary. Only a very small amount of grinds end up in the bottoms of our cups but that to me means we just drank a good cup of percolated coffee.

The percolating process is quick and I can honestly say I'll never go back to pot/drip coffee. A good percolator will change you, and this is just the one to do it. Some tips/advice for anyone new to percolator coffee: 1. You need less coffee in the basket than the booklet says or you think you need; water continously moves over the grounds, creating a really strong brew, as opposed to passing over it once and dripping down. 2. It makes *really* strong coffee; do not take that lightly. Because it passes through the grounds so many times, the caffeine (and flavor) is amplified. You've been warned. I dilute my caffeinated coffee with decaf, a hard lesson I learned after using this a few times. 3. Once the light comes on to indicate the coffee is ready, it's not. Give the water and grounds in there time to sink all the way down to the bottom for about 5 minutes, then you can pour. That's not a fault of the percolator's, thats a little tip passed down to me from my percolator elders, and now I give it to you. 4. Unless you've used a paper filter, some grounds will sink to the very bottom of the coffee, and if you empty everything into your cup on your final pour, there will be grounds in your coffee. This is normal and to be expected with any percolator. Simply don't pour the last little bit of coffee when you're getting your final cup! And last, the people complaining about the "noise" of this percolator are absolutely crazy. It's a percolator, it's *going* to make noise, but this one in particular is much more quiet than others! And enjoy the sounds it makes-- that's the sound of your most delicious cup of coffee being made. It's homey; it's a remaining sound of the past and a timeless gadget; appreciate it.

title: Finally bought after 20 years -- great coffee, but very fussy machine
body: I've been looking at this manufacturer for 20 years -- ever since Cooks Illustrated rated it the best. I finally bought one. The bottom line is it makes very good coffee, but I don't love the machine yet. I expected fussy, but after using its closest competitor (Bonavita) for years -- which is exceedingly easy to use and also makes very good coffee -- this seems a little much. There is a loose, separate cover for both the water and the grounds that have to be removed and placed somewhere (on my crowded counter) while you add water and grounds. The transfer arm that transports the water to the grounds is removable, and while it seems fairly secure, since it's press-fitted to the reservoir's silicone seal, I'm concerned that over time it will loosen and lose its seal. The brew basket has to fit into pegs, and has a spring-loaded release trap that I expect to wear out eventually. It's also complicated to clean, due to its design. The glass carafe has this bizarre funnel lid that goes to the bottom of the carafe, and is awkward to maneuver when filling it with water, so I just remove it. The warming plate surface material (some kind of plastic) has a fair amount of friction, and since one has to push up another spring-loaded device when slipping the pot under the basket, it makes it more difficult to get the pot in. It tends to bind, and you have to wiggle the pot a little to get it under. They should improve the plastic - make it more slick -- or just switch to stainless steel, which would have more slip. Washing all these individual parts will be a chore, and I think they have to be hand-washed.

title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
body: This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor)

title: Looks good in pictures and description. Return before 30 day window ends.
body: Looks good in pictures but shows it flaws quickly. I love the Corsair brand and took a chance on this chair because it looks great. Some issues I found include: lumbar cushion is too large and impractical/uncomfortable; unusable. Head cushion is fine, but taller people will have to slouch for it to fit your neck and cause lower back pain; remove it and there is no neck support at all. back cushion material is very thin and will quickly give way to the lumbar frame, which is not comfortable at all. The entire chair mechanism and controls are cheap quality. Even in the locked position the chair still rocks back and forth to a small degree. You are constantly flexing your muscles just to stay in one because of the sway. The bolt holes are flimsy and even when tightened beyond capacity, the entire chair still rocks and flexes. No stability at all. Arm rests are completely fixed in place and can only go up and down. Arm rest surface is hard and uncomfortable. Arm rests stay in place when leaning back causing your arms to completely come off the arm rest or having to stretch both arms just to stay on the armrest, another huge inconvenience and ergonomic issue. Seat cushion is just thin as the back support. Thin cheap poly stuffing across metal frames. Get ready for serious lower back issues. Unless you are a small child, this chair is not for you. Now I know why they only give you 30 days to return the item. The chair shows its issues after that window closes.

title: Glad I bought it…Well not for long
body: I was hesitant to buy this chair. Every review I read was an emotional rollercoaster. One minute it’s great, one minute it’s trash, I wasn’t sure what to believe. I decided to just commit to it and order since I’ve always wanted this chair, and it matches my Corsair peripherals. I ordered it Monday, it came Wednesday, which is pretty awesome. Everything was well packaged. Branded bags, a lot of protection surrounding the products, I was impressed. It does NOT come with physical instructions, but you can just find them online. Super straight forward install which took me a solid half an hour at most. Now, the final verdict. First sit down and I was really impressed. The bottom cushion is honestly nice, and the two back pillows work well and fit my body like a glove. I’ve already used this for a consecutive couple of hours and I’m happier than I was in my other chair. I was rocking a Respawn 110 Pro, which is very large and plush but is very cheap feeling in comparison. For those looking to get this chair, every single one of the complaints I’ve seen did NOT fit my experience. Whether it be the parts, the bolts, the cushion, whatever. But I do understand where some of these may come from. Let me advise that this chair is absolutely perfect for me. Im 5’11 and 145 so I’m not your average bodybuilder. It still has some room but just be mindful of that since it does seem like it’s meant for the “smaller” peeps. Besides that, everything feels great and is premium. It left me surprised, and I will continue to not trust reviews and just get the dang thing myself. Glad I made the decision.

title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
body: This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor)

title: This review is all over the place but informative!
body: Initially worried about the reviews I've read about the arm rests and some other things, and the price almost pushing me away from buying this chair. Finally pulling the trigger I can say with confidence they either fixed what people were talking about with the arm rests (made them closer to the chair and more adjustable) or people just expect a love seat or couch. The chair is perfect, not a single problem putting it together, I had it together in 20 mins. The chair is extremely solid and doesn't squeak at all. not only does the back of the chair recline super far like most gaming chairs, it has a separate paddle to set how far the base (place you're butt goes) reclines back to avoid having to sit back against the chair using you're weight to recline which is a massive bonus for me. some chairs require weight to recline but without being locked this chair reclines with ease. The adjustability of this chair is everything you would need. I work from home and this chair keeps me comfortable all day and all night for gaming sessions. Its a stiff chair but not too stiff, Stiff in the best way. when I first sat in it I was concerned it was going to be too stiff but after pulling 6-8 shifts for 2 weeks without standing up during, it has kept me comfortable and with 0 pain compared to my last gtp office gaming chair. after returning my Secret labs titan due to discomfort, I went from a 300$ gtp office chair to this. It has all the features you could need whether you are strict about posture, or you just wanna sit back drink a beer and watch movies or even console game its perfect. I wanted to stick to a gaming chair style but have that lumbar support and some other stuff. and I found it all in this chair. I'm 6,2 at 215-225 pounds. chair fits me perfect. I would 100% recommend trying it out if you want all the features in a gaming chair, while still keeping as much of that ergo you can with the style of chair. the pillow is actually super soft and squishy too. Its actually comfortable to use compared to other brands with really stiff pillows more for look. The chair looks leather in the mock ups, but its far from, its hard to explain, it's sort of a matte leather underarmor t shirt material. smooth and grippy but not sticky like leather. that may sound weird but in my opinion its the perfect material for a computer chair. its almost like a smoother suede material. Only negative I guess I would give them which wont effect anyone using this chair on carpet, is the wheels are pretty stiff if you dont have the weight of the chair on them. they wont freely spin if you flick the wheel with you're hand but they spin just fine. definitely not a hard floor friendly wheel, which I don't know of much other then buying roller blade computer chair wheels for commercial office spaces. all in all doesnt effect me all and the chair moves just as easily as any other on carpet. TO ANSWER SOME QUESTIONS IVE SEEN PEOPLE ASK ONLINE... 1. you cannot feel the diamond stitching at all on your back even after long sitting sessions. 2. the arm rests are more adjustable then secret labs and the gtp office chairs and not too far away from the chair (anymore?). 3. the price is steep until you feel the quality and durability of the materials they use, the weight and thickness of all the bolts, plastics, metals and fabrics show the quality. 4. how does it compare to secret labs? in my opinion the secret labs are super over hyped and over priced, yes they last a long time. but in my opinion they are super uncomfortable. for 150$ less then the titan, this chair takes the cake. All in all this chair is a 10/10 FOR ME. I know chairs fit everyone differently but I found the only chair I'm going to be sitting in until the tc600 or up comes out! sorry for the all over review if you made it this far, I just had all these questions when I was buying and I think this wraps up most of them. 500$ is alot for a chair but this is 500$ well spent in my book. I posted pictures I thought would best explain the chair. there is simply not enough reviews or info on this chair online yet with this model being less then a year old and being expensive I hope this helps you! cheers and good luck on you're chair hunt. p.s I am not sponsored by corsair although I wish I was, I just really like the chair :)

title: Great chair
body: This is is such an upgrade from my last sub $100 chair. The adjustable back support is worth the cost alone. I was hunching over in my last chair and now my posture is correct. These chairs are made of soft fabric. I am 5’4 and it adjusts to my height. There is a qr code for build instructions on the top of box when you open it. The arm rests can be adjusted multiple ways. There is a tab on each arm that lets you move them up and down. I didn't notice this at first, so I couldn't reach the arm rests till I moved them up. The box is very heavy and very large. You will need 2 people to pick it up or you can turn it on its side and roll it like i did if you don't have help. Cons: The fabric has a break-in period and might feel stiff at first, but it will adjust the more you use it. I recommend getting a memory foam cushion if this bothers you. There is a primer-like new smell but will go away in a few days. You might want to open a window during this period if it bothers you. Since the arm rests move if you pull on them, I recommend grabbing the wings near the top of the chair to move it.

title: Great chair for a killer price.
body: I have had a Secret Lab chair that I have been using for work for the past 6 years and have had my share of issues with it (their warranty is a joke). When I had to return to the office and took my Secret Lab back, I needed a chair for home. I refused to pay over $500 for a new chair. I looked into this one and got it around Christmas time for $250. At that price, this chair is a phenomenal value. It is a little smaller than my Titan XL but accommodates my 6-ft 280 Lb frame without complaining. It looks awesome. The green that I have really feels like a master chief OD green. (I'd love to embroider a Chief helmet on the back). The adjustment of the lumbar is great and I was able to make it more comfortable and supportive than my Secret Lab. My only gripe is the armrests don't lock into place. While they are great for their adjustability and range of motion, they can easily move when you are adjusting or really "in the zone." That's really the reason for 4 stars because the armrests are what you interact with the most after the seat itself.

title: NO WAY!!!
body: Definitely not worth the price. The seat feels good kind of feels like you’re sitting on a firm bubble. There are side bolsters on the seat with tubular metal so those will hurt your legs if you try to man spread. The quality of the tilt mechanism is absolutely terrible. I only weigh 160 pounds and the tension is maxed out and I still feel if I lean back I’m gonna fly out of the chair. The armrest are cool, but not good. I know a lot of people complain They’re too far forward but that is easily fixed by switching them around, the problem is they’re still not that great even after doing so. The main issue with this chair is the absolute window, licking engineering that went into the back rest. I don’t think these companies genuinely test their products before they release them, but you can 100% feel the support bar that holds the lumbar system at the top of the back rest. It is immediate as soon as you sit in the chair no it is not the lumbar itself it is a brace that holds the mechanism. Also, I am 5 foot 10 and the side bolsters of the back rest make contact with my arms in certain positions and is far from comfortable. Do not let this chair deceive you it does not hold your upper back. You get an uncomfortable bar at the middle of your back and the only other point of contact is the head pillow. Yeah let’s talk about the head pillow you could sneeze in this thing falls off. They use the weakest magnet imaginable, and the pillow feels infinitely cheaper than other companies. Please stop making chairs corsair.

Fits comfortably on my back even fully loaded — the straps are padded enough that I don’t notice it after a few hours out. Zippers feel sturdy, no snagging or sticking so far, which I was a little worried about given some tactical bags skimp there. Plenty of compartments for organizing smaller stuff (keys, wallet, cables) separately from bigger items, and it doesn’t feel bulky or oversized for everyday use despite how much it can hold. It’s also easy to throw in a car or take on the go without feeling like overkill. For the price, this feels like solid value — good build quality without the markup you’d pay for similar “tactical” branded bags. Would recommend if you want something durable that doesn’t feel like a chore to wear daily.

title: Great Travel Backpack, One Small Con
body: This is a great backpack for travel or work, and I definitely recommend it. Bagsmart knows their stuff! I bought this backpack to use specifically for when I travel because I found travel totes to be annoying—it’s so much easier to carry a backpack. This particular one has a medium capacity, it’s smaller than a typical school/college/work backpack, but bigger than a mini backpack. It had more than enough space for my travel pillow and sweatshirt in the main compartment, snacks and charging equipment in the secondary pocket, and small miscellaneous items in the front pocket. It also has a front slip pocket that’s perfect for things like keys, boarding, passes, lip balm. Overall, this bag is great. I loved that I could organize my travel necessities. My ONE qualm, and why I docked a star, is the fact that it only has one zipper pull on each of the main compartments. I know this is minor but it annoyed me enough to mention! I like being able to position the zipper opening where I prefer, and if I (or anyone) needed to lock the zippers together for travel security/anti-theft, it wouldn’t be possible. Overall a great bag.

title: HDR goodness
body: I am coming from an IPS Predator panel. I didn't chose to buy this screen because of picture quality but because I wanted a higher resolution. Coming from 1080P, so this one was within my price range. Also wanted HDR whereas my last panel didn't support it. I've been using this one for a day and a half and I must say it's eye opening what I was missing out on. Also a lot of misconception regarding miniled panels. The picture quality is just as good and even BETTER than the predator it replaced. The 180hz refresh rate is less than the 240hz it replaced but I can't notice any difference, no input lag or ghosting at all. Smooth and clear. The brightness of this screen with HDR enabled is INSANE, you just don't know what you are missing until you have tried true HDR. The colors in SDR isn't as good as my IPS panel but once you turn on HDR the colors are better than my predator monitor and insanely bright. If you find it too bright you can turn it down to whatever level pleases you. The 1152 lighting zones give this miniled a HUGE bonus to darks and bright images. Meaning very deep blacks and bright brights! I have a fairly new OLED TV and I can't see any difference between the two technologies. The color options in HDR is greyed out so you can't adjust it but I can see why this is the case. It doesn't need any adjustment at all... The colors are fantastic in HDR. To keep all the goodness of HDR not just while gaming you can turn it on for windows operating system as well. I turned it on for everything. I really did not understand what a huge difference HDR makes. Ran some identifying software Aida, and says it's putting out over 1500 knits brightness in HDR. Games just look 100% better with HDR it's no contest. I'll never go back to non HDR viewing. 1440P is the sweet spot for gaming and navigating windows. Even when HDR is on you can adjust the brightness to your liking. You will have to make certain adjustments for this panel in terms of contrast but I made all the changes within the first few minutes. Also has game setting for boosting smoothness but it's refresh rate of 180 hz is more than good enough by itself. Well done KTC for getting consumers what they want. No frills monitor and great quality!

title: Best water bottle ever!
body: This bottle hits all of the criteria for greatness. It is BPA-free, I can see through it to see how much water I drank, it is labeled clearly and with big writing to indicate how much water is left and where I should be time-wise in having drank water for the day. Like most water bottles, it has a flip top dust cover and it is easily lockable so no water spills out. Unlike some water bottles, it has an extra hole at the top under the dust cover that lets out air so that you don't drink a bunch of air with your water. Unlike most water bottles, it has two handy ways to hold the bottle. It has both a hard loop on top for folk like me who hold the bottle with one finger (that makes it easy to set the bottle down, unlike with the cloth strap that it also provides which otherwise can be a nice way to carry it too. It easily fits into any car or standard cupholder. It is dishwasher friendly (though make sure the strap is captured on the bottom level of the dishwasher (like looping it around a fork) so that it doesn't get burned. If you're wondering about glass bottles, I've bought them too, but these are lighter, a bit shorter, and you don't have to worry about breaking them if you drop them. Also, the glass water bottles don't tend to have all of the features described above. Last, I like that it offers multiple colors, as in drinking my 64 oz/day, I use one color to signify my first bottle and the other to signify my second because I used to forget if I'd had one or two bottles in any given day. In short, I have bought many water bottles, and this is the best of them all! It's also cheap - well priced for the value.

The next day (Day 2), I checked it in the morning: still a lot of ice. I checked it again that night (still a very large "clump" of ice). The following day (Day 3), I again checked in the morning to find there were still a few little ice cubes still floating in the bottle. WOW! When I will be traveling in a hot environment in our car for an upcoming trip, I expect the bottle to at least keep the ice and water cold throughout each day of travel. I will do the same thing every day of our trip to ensure I have something cold to sip. Good job, Encool! I am very pleased! So pleased that I immediately purchased a 2nd bottle for my husband! It feels like it is made of great quality. The handle is wide enough for my four fingers to grasp. Something I hadn't noticed is that the handle area closest to the bottle lid isn't just a 90-degree angle; it is made with a 45-degree angle at each side so your fingers rest more comfortably when holding the bottle. The lid has both the straw-sip and the chug options, and work great. I turned the full bottle on its side all night and there were no leaks. This may just be the perfect water bottle for us!

title: Falls short to Yeti but still nice!
body: I wanted this Stanley to be my reason to turn away from Yeti. I love the modern design, the all black, the non-fixed handle that can be tightened to be more fixed/harder to move, and the 50 oz capacity. It was nice to see that the bottle had 4 extra oz of capacity at the same price as Yeti’s 46 oz bottle. I need to drink lots of water throughout the day and the large capacity is awesome. The lightness was originally a selling point for me; while it can hold an astonishingly large 50 oz, since the bottle is relatively light in weight, it doesn’t feel too heavy to carry a full bottle around. However, where it excels in lightness it falls short in quality. It is glaringly lower quality than Yeti’s 46 oz bottle. This Stanley has thinner metal leading to poorer insulation. What frustrated me the most was realizing how much thinner the coating was compared to Yeti; I accidentally dinged it with a fork while heating up my lunch and chipped it! I’ve dropped my Yetis dozens of times and hit them with everything from forks and knives to granite countertops and haven’t had an issue with them chipping under light use. I even noticed it will take on light scratches from the plastic buckles on my lunch box if I let them touch while in my bag. Seriously poor coating. However, getting back to the pros, the leak resistance is great and when properly closed you can rest assured you won’t have spillage or leakage. Also the straw on this bottle is much nicer than the straws on Yeti bottles; less resistance and simply easier to sip. In the end, it’s a great water bottle that has a cool modern look and a huge capacity. Overall this comes in at 4/5 stars with only one star being lost to the thinner metal and thinner coating. I would still suggest getting the Yeti 46 oz instead for the thicker metal and coating as it will likely last longer and endure more.

title: Is it possible for a water bottle to improve your life?
body: I don't know what kind of mad scientist they have working for Owala, but can we get this guy working on improving other things, like those gas pumps that always shut off every $.05 cents, or maybe invent a cell phone screen protector that doesn't crack a week after you put it on? Seriously, what an amazing design they have. I love the Owala spouts. I detest water bottles with straws, except for Owala. These things are so pleasant to drink out of. Also, this lid is fantastic, it's leak proof, easy to remove (Stanley, take a look, this is better), and that little string loop thing goes great over your middle finger. That's the strongest point, and if someone messes with you swing that thing like a club! Seriously, don't go around just hitting people, but as a self-defense item this will work! It kept my ice water nice and cold today. They claim you can put other stuff in here, but really, why would you? It's such a fantastic water bottle. I guess if you wanted to load it up with coffee, tea, soda, or any number of adult beverages that's up to you. I just don't want to stain up the inside. The 18 ounce fits perfectly in my backpack's water bottle pocket. I have the Bellroy Transit Workpack Pro 28L. I bought this to take with me when I fly. Empty water bottles are allowed thru security, then fill it up after going through security. It'll save you a bunch on bottled water. If you want something easy to carry, fits any cup holder, and can hold enough water to quench your thirst for a reasonable amount of time the 18 ounce is perfect. If you're one of those people that likes to carry enough water for a full day of hiking on the AT this probably isn't for you. For the rest of us it's perfect! Great job Owala!

title: The best water bottle I've ever owned. Seriously.
body: This is the absolute best water bottle I have ever owned. Happened upon one in the thrift store, and was stunned at how long it kept my drink cold on a scorching hot day (freezing cold, with ice still in it, 24 hours later). Made of sturdy materials, which is great, because it gets used a LOT. Love the spout - I hate cleaning the straws and the tops with tiny holes, and feel like there is place for ick to grow in them - but I feel like when I wash this, it's CLEAN. It's the right size (24 oz) for me, and easy to carry with the handle, even when I am also carrying a camp chair, a camera bag, a food cooler and all the rest of the detritus you bring with you to youth sports games. Seal is excellent - it could be knocked on the ground at a baseball game by a 70 mph fastball and not lose the seal (do not ask how I know this). The silicone seal does not seem to degrade with repeated washing, either - the thrift store one is from 3 years ago (and who knows how much longer it was used before that) and still going strong. I loved the thrift store purchase so much, I did the research and found the same model online (albeit a new, different color), and could not believe they were so on sale (19.99, I think). A true bargain. And now mine won't get stolen by my kid every time I put it down - we'll each have our own. I'm gonna buy one for my mom and husband, too. Seriously - this is one of the few products in life that you will like even better than you thought you would.

title: Insulated Water Bottle is Definitely a Better Choice than the Non-Insulated Model
body: Actually holds cold all day, leak proof, the insulated 32-oz. size fits in the larger cup holes in a Ford Explorer and a 2014 F-150 (the cupholder in the middle closer to the floor), and best of all, there is NO plastic touching the water or tea or whatever you store in it - it's stainless steel all around, including the screw-on top. There is a small circular seal of what appears to be silicone at the top of that screw-on top, but it isn't in contact with the liquid inside this insulated water bottle. I also tested how well it would insulate hot liquids by boiling some water, steeping tea, and then filling the water bottle with hot tea - and it stayed hot all day. It is stamped 304 in the bottom of the inside of the water bottle, indicating that this is supposed to be 304 stainless steel, which is supposed to be the same as 18/8 stainless steel - non-magnetic. Feel free to comment below if you know of a water bottle with superior quality steel out there, but thus far it has held up well and it's the best water bottle I've tried. The stainless steel exterior finish option still has a decent grip, I also bought one in green and it has a very good gripping surface as well. These seem to be designed to be carried by the handle that is part of the screw-on top - which also doubles as a more ergonomic way to open the bottle at the end of the day. As for the blue one, the color seemed a bit darker than it had appeared on my screen, more slate/grayish with some navy, so I didn't keep the blue one. The green was very much the green as it appeared on my screen, and the stainless steel finish was my husband's favorite. It's a great value, and I love how it can work for both cold and hot liquids. I definitely recommend this insulated water bottle over their non-insulated model - the last thing you want is to return to your vehicle on a hot day and have your previously chilled water warm, or your warm tea cool when it's cold weather. This insulated model works great outdoors and indoors, and if you're running errands or you're going to be driving and just want to leave your water bottle in the car, it holds up well.

title: The best water bottle I've ever owned. Seriously.
body: This is the absolute best water bottle I have ever owned. Happened upon one in the thrift store, and was stunned at how long it kept my drink cold on a scorching hot day (freezing cold, with ice still in it, 24 hours later). Made of sturdy materials, which is great, because it gets used a LOT. Love the spout - I hate cleaning the straws and the tops with tiny holes, and feel like there is place for ick to grow in them - but I feel like when I wash this, it's CLEAN. It's the right size (24 oz) for me, and easy to carry with the handle, even when I am also carrying a camp chair, a camera bag, a food cooler and all the rest of the detritus you bring with you to youth sports games. Seal is excellent - it could be knocked on the ground at a baseball game by a 70 mph fastball and not lose the seal (do not ask how I know this). The silicone seal does not seem to degrade with repeated washing, either - the thrift store one is from 3 years ago (and who knows how much longer it was used before that) and still going strong. I loved the thrift store purchase so much, I did the research and found the same model online (albeit a new, different color), and could not believe they were so on sale (19.99, I think). A true bargain. And now mine won't get stolen by my kid every time I put it down - we'll each have our own. I'm gonna buy one for my mom and husband, too. Seriously - this is one of the few products in life that you will like even better than you thought you would.

I love that not only are they leak proof, but the texture of the bottle has a slightly bumpy feel to add friction so you are less likely to drop it. I also love that the spout is not a straw. It is molded at the top to act like a water bottle but has a piece that acts as a barrier to guide the water into your mouth rather than just pouring out. Will make drinking out of it immediately gratifying without being messy which is exactly what we need to survive our Disney vacation this August. Water stayed cold overnight with just a few ice cubes in each. The 18 Oz is perfect for kids or adults who need a more compact water bottle.

title: Top needs to go back more!
body: My friends were trying to convince we to buy an owala, but the color I wanted wasn’t available in the 20 oz, so I decided to give this a try. I am so glad I did, because I actually like this one better! Looking at them both, they are very similar in design, but one main difference is that to drink from the o straw, you sip from the same opening where you free sip. This one has a straw piece that flips up behind the free sip area, which I like better. The cap seems sturdier, and the when the handle is down you can still press the button to open the cap to free sip. On the o, the handle prevents you from pressing the button, so you need to lift the handle to open the top to drink from it—I guess whether this is a pro or con depends on whether you want the button to be blocked or not. The button on this one is also easier to press to pop the top up. It does not leak at all, it fits in my car cup holder, and it kept my water cold for the 6 hours it took me to drink it. Even though I balked at spending $20 on a water bottle, it’s still cheaper than the other one by a fair amount, and I love the color—I will definitely be buying more in the other sizes!

title: You won’t need to rely on another brand
body: I come from the cheap Walmart store cups that work for a little while but for one reason or another they break on me. Then I tried the “other” big brand cups and they’re cool but they aren’t rugged enough or quite built for what I need, they are just pretty. Then I looked into Yeti and I’ve finally found my love. I’m a blue collar worker who has serious blue collar needs, I’m also a hiker and camper this fits the bill perfectly for all the above. I love this black stone color and texture but they only had it in 18oz which I was afraid of because that seemed a bit too small, but there was a science that went into the size of the chug cap on this cup. Somehow the liquid to ice ratio that comes out the hole makes it feel perfectly enough and it ends up lasting longer than expected! Somehow it is enough for the colder months at work, however I’m still going to go a size up for my next purchase to 26oz for the hotter months just because I like how slim they managed to make that size cup and of course it will hold more liquid. I love that this 18oz is not heavy at all while clipped to my medium sized sling backpack when my backpack is full, it can also fit very slim inside for the days that are too cold to carry it(I don’t have side pockets on my bag unfortunately). It stays cold for a full shift and then some, I drink my hot drinks pretty quick so I can’t really say much on that but so far I’ve gotten at least 4 hours of keeping hot drinks hot. This cup is 100% leakproof! And also I love that Yeti offers you different methods to drink by purchasing different cross compatible caps to all their cups. This or ANY Yeti cup will be the perfect gift for anyone looking for reliability and durability! Just get one and prepare to be addicted!

title: Great value and quality
body: I'll start out by saying I rarely give five stars, t-shirts that fit well are difficult for me to find. I usually go through several Brands before I find one I like and then I have to try several sizes to settle on one. With all of that being said, the shirts are a great quality for the price especially, and they are true to size. The fabric, stitching, and packaging are great for the price you're paying. I would consider these right in between a muscle fit and a slim fit, flattering in the arms and chest but not too tight in the waist, and the length seems to be just right. I wasn't really sold by the pictures of people trying them on but when I got the shirts in hand they seem to fit way better and look much nicer. If I have one thing that I could point out that isn't a complete positive it would be that the neck could be just slightly tighter and a bit more sturdy but that's really nitpicking because the neck does not sag at all, after a wash this might tighten up slightly and all the shirts seem to be identical and well made whereas usually when I order there might be one or two shirts that just aren't up to par. I got a 12 pack of the black and I will be ordering more for my day-to-day t-shirts, including a 12 pack of the whites. For a little perspective in rating these shirts, I used to buy the Haynes that were on Amazon and (I've noticed that the quality had gone down a bit) but those shirts usually run anywhere from 8 to $12 a piece and these are right up there with them if not better.

title: Great value and quality
body: I'll start out by saying I rarely give five stars, t-shirts that fit well are difficult for me to find. I usually go through several Brands before I find one I like and then I have to try several sizes to settle on one. With all of that being said, the shirts are a great quality for the price especially, and they are true to size. The fabric, stitching, and packaging are great for the price you're paying. I would consider these right in between a muscle fit and a slim fit, flattering in the arms and chest but not too tight in the waist, and the length seems to be just right. I wasn't really sold by the pictures of people trying them on but when I got the shirts in hand they seem to fit way better and look much nicer. If I have one thing that I could point out that isn't a complete positive it would be that the neck could be just slightly tighter and a bit more sturdy but that's really nitpicking because the neck does not sag at all, after a wash this might tighten up slightly and all the shirts seem to be identical and well made whereas usually when I order there might be one or two shirts that just aren't up to par. I got a 12 pack of the black and I will be ordering more for my day-to-day t-shirts, including a 12 pack of the whites. For a little perspective in rating these shirts, I used to buy the Haynes that were on Amazon and (I've noticed that the quality had gone down a bit) but those shirts usually run anywhere from 8 to $12 a piece and these are right up there with them if not better.
